blueprint.name: BNK on a NEW disconnected IBM ROKS cluster (private registry + F5 License Proxy)
blueprint.description: Provision a NEW IBM ROKS cluster with its own VPC and Transit Gateway and NO worker Internet egress, then install BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes onto it from a private registry you have already mirrored, licensed through an F5 License Proxy. Build the mirror and the proxy first with the Harbor and FLP blueprints. The cwc-guard module is deliberately absent: F5's f5-spk-cwc Multi-Attach deadlock only arises on a cluster that has already run BNK, which a freshly created cluster never has.

outcomes: The BNK supply chain replicated into your private registry and verified
An existing air-gapped ROKS cluster adopted over the Transit Gateway
BNK installed with every image from the mirror and the License CR Active via the FLP

prerequisites.description: An IBM Cloud credential template on the project. Region and resource group inherit from it.
A running F5 License Proxy the cluster can reach privately — deploy one with the 'Deploying F5 License Proxy as an IBM Cloud VSI' blueprint, then paste its external_endpoint and root_ca_b64 here.
An orchestration COS bucket holding the FAR auth tarball and the subscription JWT — the only artifacts not served from the mirror.

input_summary.label: Two phases
input_summary.value: Mirror (init -> registry replicate --target generic -> registry verify) then Install (cluster register -> bnk up -> bnk status), sharing one deployment workspace — the same split, and the same shared state, as the demo's two Argo Workflows over one PVC.

input_summary.label: Registry trust
input_summary.value: roksbnkctl captures the mirror's CA from its served chain during replicate, trusts it for the operator's own crane/helm/terraform pulls, and installs it on every worker node via its registry-trust DaemonSet before any image pull. Requires runner >= v1.33.0.

input_summary.label: Known gap
input_summary.value: The demo pairs `bnk up` with a cwc-guard sidecar that clears F5's ReadWriteOnce Multi-Attach deadlock on a REUSED cluster. A Forge container step is a single container with no sidecar, so that guard is not reproduced here — on a cluster where BNK was previously installed, licensing may stall until f5-spk-cwc is cycled by hand.

required.name: prefix
required.label: Resource prefix (and cluster name)
required.description: Prefix for every IBM resource created here. The ROKS cluster is named exactly this — roksbnkctl names a new cluster after the prefix.

required.name: region
required.label: IBM Cloud region
required.description: Region the cluster lives in. Inherits from the selected credential template.

required.name: resource_group
required.label: Resource group
required.description: IBM Cloud resource group. Inherits from the selected credential template.

required.name: registry_generic_host
required.label: Private registry host
required.description: The private registry (e.g. Harbor) BNK's charts and images are mirrored into and pulled from. For an air-gapped cluster this is its PRIVATE IP or DNS name, reached over the Transit Gateway.

required.name: registry_password
required.label: Registry password
required.description: Password / access token for that user. Stored base64 in the workspace config, never logged.

required.name: flp_external_url
required.label: FLP endpoint
required.description: Licensing endpoint of an F5 License Proxy this cluster does NOT own — `flp output flp_external_endpoint` on the workspace that does.

required.name: flp_root_ca_b64
required.label: FLP root CA (base64)
required.description: That proxy's base64 root CA, which the cluster's CWC must trust — `flp output flp_root_ca`. Already base64: it is stored verbatim.

required.name: cos_bucket
required.label: Supply-chain COS bucket
required.description: Orchestration COS bucket holding the FAR auth tarball and the subscription JWT. The runner has no local copies, so it resolves them from here; buckets provisioned by `roksbnkctl init` carry a per-account suffix (bnk-artifacts-<account>).

required.name: registry_ca_b64
required.label: Registry CA (base64)
required.description: Base64 PEM of the private registry's CA. v1.35.0 REFUSES to auto-capture a self-signed mirror's CA over the wire, so supply it here (or pin it below) — this is the CA you generated for the registry.

required.name: cluster_vpc_cidr
required.label: Cluster VPC address block
required.description: Address block for the new cluster's VPC (/18 or larger). REQUIRED here: this cluster shares a Transit Gateway with the private mirror, and IBM's default 'auto' gives every VPC in the region the same prefixes — a second cluster on that gateway would overlap and the gateway would blackhole one of them. Pick a block no other attached VPC uses, e.g. 10.242.0.0/16.

optional.name: subscription_jwt_file
optional.label: Subscription JWT object name
optional.description: Object name of the subscription JWT in the bucket. Blank = subscription.jwt.

optional.name: far_auth_file
optional.label: FAR auth object name
optional.description: Object name of the FAR auth tarball in the bucket. Blank = f5-far-auth-key.tgz.

optional.name: cos_instance
optional.label: Supply-chain COS instance
optional.description: COS instance holding the FAR auth key + subscription JWT. Blank = bnk-supply-chain.

optional.name: openshift_version
optional.label: OpenShift version
optional.description: OpenShift version for the new cluster.

optional.name: workers_per_zone
optional.label: Workers per zone
optional.description: Across three zones; 2 gives a 6-worker cluster.

optional.name: registry_repo_prefix
optional.label: Registry repository prefix
optional.description: Project / repository prefix inside the mirror (a Harbor project, an Artifactory repo key).

optional.name: registry_username
optional.label: Registry username
optional.description: Username the mirror is pushed to and pulled from.

optional.name: cos_region
optional.label: Supply-chain COS region
optional.description: Region of that bucket. Blank = us-south. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: registry_cos_name
optional.label: Registry COS instance name
optional.description: Overrides the registry COS instance `cluster register` looks for. Blank = probe <prefix>-registry-cos, <cluster>-registry-cos, <cluster>-cos. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: manifest_version
optional.label: BNK manifest version
optional.description: BNK manifest release to install. Blank = the roksbnkctl default.

optional.name: registry_ca_sha256
optional.label: Registry CA SHA-256 pin
optional.description: SHA-256 pin of the registry's served chain, enforced during the TLS handshake. Accepts bare hex, sha256:…, colon-separated, or raw `openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256` output. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: bnkforge_url
optional.label: BNK Forge URL
optional.description: Register the adopted cluster with a BNK Forge instance so it appears on the Kubernetes page (e.g. https://forge.example.com). Blank = skip registration. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: bnkforge_username
optional.label: BNK Forge username
optional.description: Login for that Forge. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: bnkforge_password
optional.label: BNK Forge password
optional.description: Password for that login. Reaches the step as an environment variable only, never on the command line. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: bnkforge_project
optional.label: BNK Forge project
optional.description: BNK Forge project to register the cluster into. Filled automatically with THIS project's name, so the cluster appears on the Kubernetes page of the project you deployed and its scans can be watched as BNK installs.

optional.name: bnkforge_insecure
optional.label: Skip Forge TLS verification
optional.description: Set true only for a Forge with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false — verification stays on unless you opt out.

optional.name: flp_namespace
optional.label: FLP namespace
optional.description: Kubernetes namespace the F5 License Proxy client resources go into. Blank keeps the default the subscription JWT implies. Leave blank to use roksbnkctl's default.

optional.name: ibmcloud_api_key
optional.label: IBM Cloud API key
optional.description: Resolved from the project's credential template when the project is created. Not entered by hand.

optional.name: reachability_retry_seconds
optional.label: Mirror/FLP reachability retry budget (seconds)
optional.description: Raised from the roksbnkctl default of 180s because THIS blueprint attaches the Transit Gateway in the same run as the install: cluster-create attaches it, then bnk-install probes minutes later, before IBM has finished programming routes. Measured on a real run: a probe 73s after attach reported no route to a mirror that was reachable moments later. Lower it only for a gateway that was attached long beforehand.

optional.name: reachability_timeout_seconds
optional.label: Mirror/FLP reachability overall timeout (seconds)
optional.description: Raised alongside the retry budget. roksbnkctl clamps this above the retry value, so it can never be smaller than the time it has been told to keep retrying.

optional.name: cluster_vpc_id
optional.label: Existing cluster VPC (id)
optional.description: Place the new cluster in a VPC you already have, instead of creating one (roksbnkctl v1.43.0+). Blank creates the VPC, which is the default. Use this where address space is allocated centrally. Adopting a VPC that already reaches the registry and the License Proxy is also what lets you leave the Transit Gateway blank here. Leave 'Existing cluster subnets' blank to have roksbnkctl create the three zone subnets inside the adopted VPC.

optional.name: existing_transit_gateway
optional.label: Existing Transit Gateway (name or id)
optional.description: The gateway the private mirror and F5 License Proxy already sit on. Supply it when this blueprint creates the cluster's VPC — a VPC built from nothing has no route to the registry it must pull every image from, so the gateway is what gives it one. Leave it blank only when the cluster's VPC can already reach both, which in practice means adopting a VPC via 'Existing cluster VPC (id)' that shares or is peered to their network. `bnk up` proves every node can reach the registry and the proxy before installing, so a wrong answer fails fast and says so.

optional.name: existing_subnet_ids
optional.label: Existing cluster subnets (ids, comma-separated)
optional.description: Adopt pre-created subnets instead of letting roksbnkctl cut them inside the VPC (roksbnkctl v1.44.0+). Comma-separated subnet ids in ZONE ORDER, e.g. 0717-a,0717-b,0717-c. Requires 'Existing cluster VPC (id)' — roksbnkctl refuses a subnet adopted independently of the VPC that contains it. Blank creates the subnets, which is the default.

modules.name: roksbnkctl Cluster Create
modules.description: Create the VPC and ROKS cluster with no worker egress, attach it to the existing Transit Gateway, then register the cluster with BNK Forge — registration runs first, so it is visible and monitorable while BNK installs.

modules.name: roksbnkctl BNK Install
modules.description: init -> cluster register -> bnk up -> bnk status, pulling from the mirror and licensing via the FLP.
